thread:
Asha Patel: Heads up — ran into a quoting snag for a mid-market POC. New rate table v3 dropped yesterday and the SKU mapping doesn't match the legacy POC invoice schema. Customer asking for the original commit tiers to be honored for the POC period. Anyone have a quick playbook?
Marco Ruiz: Can you paste the exact SKU mismatch? we might be able to do a temporary mapping on our end.
Asha Patel: Yep: customer was quoted 'dedicated-poc-50' but v3 consolidated to 'dedicated-base' with different commit thresholds. Snippet: ```quoted_sku: dedicated-poc-50\nrate_v3: dedicated-base (min_commit 1000)```
Priya Desai: If we honor the old tiers for this POC we need to flag it as a one-off credit. Finance needs the deal desk ticket + start/end dates. Also need to confirm revenue recognition won't be impacted.
Lily Chen: Legal: fine with one-off exceptions if sales gets signoff and we capture terms in an amendment. We should limit to POCs < 90 days and add a clause: "temporary pricing exception, non-precedential."
Jon Park: Product: worth noting that the new SKU change is intentional to simplify autoscaling. But we can support a compatibility mapping for short-term POCs. Noted for future docs.
deal-desk-bot: New Deal Desk ticket created: DD-2147. Please attach the customer quote and POC timeline.
Asha Patel: DD-2147 — attached quote and customer's signed SOW in the ticket. Customer requests that the effective date be backdated to the POC start on 2026-03-01. Thoughts?
Marco Ruiz: Backdating OK only if we have exec approval. Otherwise set exception start = ticket approval date. We should avoid retroactive billing adjustments. @Priya?
Priya Desai: Agree with Marco. No retroactive revenue changes without finance exec sign-off. We can do an exception effective from approval and prorate the first invoice to match the originally quoted economics for the remaining POC days.
Lily Chen: Legal also prefers approval-forward. We can draft a 1-paragraph addendum that references the SOW and states exception effective on approval date, expires after 60 days from approval.
Asha Patel: Customer is pressing for the original numbers for the whole POC. Can we offer a compromise: honor legacy tiers for the remaining POC period, approval required by EOD tomorrow, and include a hard expiration?
Marco Ruiz: I'm fine to approve in deal-desk if finance ok. Priya, if you give the greenlight I'll mark DD-2147 as approved conditional on the addendum.
Priya Desai: Conditional greenlight. Finance will accept the proration approach and one-time credit treatment. Need GL code and expected ARR impact estimate in the ticket.
Lily Chen: I'll drop a 1-paragraph addendum into DD-2147 and ping legal review channel.
Jon Park: Action item for product/docs: add a short note in the internal rate card KB about "compatibility mappings" so sales doesn't get surprised next time.
Asha Patel: Cool — can we also get a quick internal announcement in #sales with the approved exception text once DD-2147 is closed? I'll want CSMs and AE to reference it. :+1:
Marco Ruiz: Will do. If all good here I'll approve DD-2147 after Priya confirms GL code.
Priya Desai: GL code: POC-CREDIT-01. I've added ARR impact estimate (~$4.2k run-rate deferral) to DD-2147. Approving pending addendum.
deal-desk-bot: DD-2147 status updated: APPROVED (conditional: signed addendum added).
Lily Chen: Addendum uploaded to ticket. Legal sign-off complete.
Asha Patel: Thanks team — will inform customer that we can honor legacy tiers for the remaining POC period, exception effective on approval date, expires 60 days later. Will post summary in #sales after I update DD-2147 with the acceptance email.
Marco Ruiz: Thanks — please cc me on the acceptance. I'll follow up to ensure internal rate table docs get the compatibility note. :memo:
Jon Park: I'll create the KB item and tag it 'rate-schedule-compatibility' so it's searchable.
Asha Patel: Closing loop: customer accepted via email, uploaded to DD-2147. Posting summary to #sales now.
_meta: generated for dataset: slack sales thread about rate schedule compatibility and POC exceptions
